exposure: second-trimester lipid profiles (triglycerides, LDL-C, total cholesterol, HDL-C)
cohort: 300 pregnant women aged 18-35 years, divided equally into hyperlipidaemic (n=150) and normolipidemic (n=150) groups based on second-trimester lipid profiles.
finding: Maternal hyperlipidaemia, particularly elevated triglycerides and LDL-C, was significantly associated with increased preeclampsia risk.
